title: Follow one web request
where: Your Windows host · lab notebook
expected: Your diagram separates visitor, DMZ, private application and private AD/management zones with one approved HTTPS route.

title: Choose local practice before Azure
where: Your Windows host · lab notebook
fields: No Azure compute or gateway bill
expected: The plan is local and isolated. Azure is a later design comparison, not a resource deployment.

title: Reserve four networks without changing the domain controllers
where: Windows host · VMware Virtual Network Editor and lab notebook
expected: Your inventory shows unique addresses, unchanged DC01/DC02 and no overlapping subnets.

title: Prepare the VM images and package tools
where: Windows host · Workstation Pro; Linux guest consoles during preparation
command:
sudo dnf upgrade --refresh -y
sudo dnf install -y nginx openssl curl tcpdump open-vm-tools fuse3 policycoreutils-python-utils
sudo systemctl enable --now vmtoolsd
expected: The guests are prepared, powered off and ready to be attached to isolated networks.

title: Create the four isolated switches
where: Windows host · VMware Workstation Pro → Edit → Virtual Network Editor
expected: VMnet2/3/4/5 are isolated host-only /24 networks with DHCP off. Only VMnet2 has the intended host management adapter.

title: Move only the host management adapter
where: Windows 10 host · Run → ncpa.cpl
fields: Blank on this virtual management adapter
expected: The host VMnet2 adapter is 10.50.0.254 and does not conflict with the future FW01 .1 address.

title: Attach the VMs and record their MAC addresses
where: Workstation Pro · each powered-off VM → Settings → Network Adapter
expected: The saved four-zone MAC/NIC inventory has four FW01 adapters and one adapter on each server/client.

title: Install OPNsense on FW01
where: FW01 VMware console · OPNsense installer
expected: FW01 boots from disk with WAN, LAN, OPT1 and OPT2 mapped to the correct recorded MACs.

title: Set the firewall’s four addresses
where: FW01 console · Set interface IP address
expected: The host reaches FW01 on 10.50.0.1 and all four interface addresses match the diagram.

title: Label the interfaces and allow the lab’s private outside addresses
where: Windows host browser · FW01 Interfaces
fields: Unchecked for this isolated test network
Review / uncheck only for lab if required
expected: The DMZ is enabled, the test outside interface accepts the planned private lab addresses, and management is confined to PRIVATE.

title: Keep an explicit administrator doorway
where: Windows host browser · Firewall → Aliases, then Rules [new] / interface rules
expected: Only the explicit administrator management path is retained; the broad LAN-to-any rules are disabled.

title: Allow one private web service from the proxy
where: Windows host browser · Firewall → Rules → DMZ
expected: DMZ_PROXY_TO_IIS_443 is above DMZ_DENY_OTHER, and there is no broad DMZ-to-private allow.

title: Give the new private server its address
where: IIS-DMZ01 guest console · Windows Server 2019 → ncpa.cpl
expected: IIS-DMZ01 is a workgroup VM at 10.80.0.40/24 with gateway 10.80.0.1 and exactly one VMnet5 NIC.

title: Install IIS and create a clearly named practice site
where: IIS-DMZ01 · Windows PowerShell as Administrator
command:
if ($env:COMPUTERNAME -ne 'IIS-DMZ01') { throw 'Wrong VM. Stop here.' } Install-WindowsFeature Web-Server -IncludeManagementTools Import-Module WebAdministration New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path C:\inetpub\dmz-lab -Force '

CloudSeam DMZ lab

Private IIS backend: IIS-DMZ01

' | Set-Content C:\inetpub\dmz-lab\index.html Stop-Website 'Default Web Site' New-Website -Name 'DMZ-Lab' -PhysicalPath C:\inetpub\dmz-lab -IPAddress 127.0.0.1 -Port 8080 (Invoke-WebRequest http://127.0.0.1:8080 -UseBasicParsing).StatusCode
expected: The local health request returns the CloudSeam training page from the DMZ-Lab site.

title: Bind HTTPS and export only the public certificate
where: IIS-DMZ01 · elevated PowerShell, then IIS Manager → DMZ-Lab → Bindings
command:
$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate -DnsName 'iis-backend.cloudseam.tech' -CertStoreLocation 'Cert:\LocalMachine\My' -FriendlyName 'DMZ-Lab backend' -KeyAlgorithm RSA -KeyLength 3072 -HashAlgorithm SHA256 -NotAfter (Get-Date).AddDays(30)
New-WebBinding -Name 'DMZ-Lab' -Protocol https -IPAddress '10.80.0.40' -Port 443 -HostHeader 'iis-backend.cloudseam.tech' -SslFlags 1
(Get-WebBinding -Name 'DMZ-Lab' -Protocol https).AddSslCertificate($cert.Thumbprint, 'My')
New-Item -ItemType Directory C:\DMZ-Lab -Force
$pem = '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----' + "`r`n" + [Convert]::ToBase64String($cert.RawData, [System.Base64FormattingOptions]::InsertLineBreaks) + "`r`n-----END CERTIFICATE-----`r`n"
$pem | Set-Content C:\DMZ-Lab\backend-public.pem -Encoding Ascii
expected: The correct SNI HTTPS binding exists, and backend-public.pem contains only the backend’s public certificate.

title: Restrict the Windows firewall and stage the public certificate
where: IIS-DMZ01 · elevated PowerShell; Windows host → Workstation shared folder settings
command:
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'DMZ-Lab HTTPS from proxy only' -Direction Inbound -Action Allow -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 443 -RemoteAddress 10.60.0.10 -Profile Any
Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'DMZ-Lab HTTPS from proxy only' | Get-NetFirewallAddressFilter
# Inspect other inbound web allows on this dedicated VM before disabling them.
Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Inbound -Enabled True -Action Allow | Where-Object DisplayName -Match 'World Wide Web|HTTPS|HTTP' | Select-Object Name,DisplayName,Enabled
expected: The Windows HTTPS rule is scoped to 10.60.0.10, and only the public backend PEM is staged for the proxy.

title: Set PROXY01’s DMZ address
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console
command:
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname proxy01.cloudseam.tech
nmcli connection show
# Replace YOUR_CONNECTION with the exact Ethernet profile name above.
sudo nmcli connection modify "YOUR_CONNECTION" ipv4.method manual ipv4.addresses 10.60.0.10/24 ipv4.gateway 10.60.0.1 ipv4.dns "" ipv6.method disabled
sudo nmcli connection up "YOUR_CONNECTION"
ip -4 address
ip -4 route
timedatectl
expected: PROXY01 has only 10.60.0.10/24 on its Ethernet NIC and uses 10.60.0.1 as gateway.

title: Copy the pinned backend certificate and prove the private HTTPS hop
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console; Workstation Options → Shared Folders
command:
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/dmz-transfer
sudo vmhgfs-fuse .host:/DMZ-Transfer /mnt/dmz-transfer -o allow_other
sudo cp /mnt/dmz-transfer/backend-public.pem /etc/pki/tls/certs/iis-backend.pem
curl --cacert /etc/pki/tls/certs/iis-backend.pem --resolve iis-backend.cloudseam.tech:443:10.80.0.40 --connect-timeout 5 https://iis-backend.cloudseam.tech/
expected: A verified curl request from PROXY01 reaches the private IIS page and a matching narrow firewall pass is logged.

title: Create the visitor-facing lab certificate
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console
command:
sudo openssl req -x509 -nodes -newkey rsa:3072 -sha256 -days 30 -keyout /etc/pki/tls/private/dmz-front.key -out /etc/pki/tls/certs/dmz-front.crt -subj "/CN=app-dmz.cloudseam.tech" -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:app-dmz.cloudseam.tech"
sudo chmod 600 /etc/pki/tls/private/dmz-front.key
openssl x509 -in /etc/pki/tls/certs/dmz-front.crt -noout -subject -dates -ext subjectAltName
sudo cp /etc/pki/tls/certs/dmz-front.crt /mnt/dmz-transfer/proxy-public.crt
expected: The front certificate has the correct SAN and dates; the front private key stays root-only on PROXY01.

title: Install the exact NGINX HTTPS proxy configuration
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console / text editor
expected: nginx -t reports a valid configuration with upstream certificate verification enabled.

title: Start the service without disabling host protections
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console
command:
sudo setsebool -P httpd_can_network_connect 1
sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="10.70.0.10/32" service name="https" accept'
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
sudo systemctl enable --now nginx
systemctl is-active nginx
getenforce
sudo ss -lntp | grep ':443'
expected: SELinux is enforcing, firewalld has the scoped visitor HTTPS rule, and NGINX is active on the DMZ listener.

title: Give the visitor its isolated outside address
where: TEST01 · AlmaLinux 9 GNOME Settings → Network
command:
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname test01.cloudseam.tech
ip -4 address
ip -4 route
expected: TEST01 is 10.70.0.10/24 with one VMnet4 NIC and gateway 10.70.0.1.

title: Forward outside TCP 443 to the DMZ proxy
where: Windows host browser · FW01 → Firewall → NAT → Destination NAT / Port Forward
expected: One outside TCP 443 forward points to PROXY01, with its narrow pass rule; IIS has no outside forward.

title: Give the visitor only the public trust certificate
where: TEST01 · AlmaLinux Terminal; temporary VMware shared folder
command:
mkdir -p ~/dmz-lab
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/dmz-transfer
sudo vmhgfs-fuse .host:/DMZ-Transfer /mnt/dmz-transfer -o allow_other
cp /mnt/dmz-transfer/proxy-public.crt ~/dmz-lab/
openssl x509 -in ~/dmz-lab/proxy-public.crt -noout -fingerprint -sha256
sudo umount /mnt/dmz-transfer
expected: TEST01 has the matching front public certificate and all temporary shared folders are disabled.

title: Make a real verified request through the whole path
where: TEST01 · AlmaLinux Terminal
expected: The request succeeds with TLS verification and returns the page created on private IIS through PROXY01.

title: Test direct outside access to the backend
where: TEST01 · AlmaLinux Terminal; FW01 Live View
command:
timeout 5 bash -c '</dev/tcp/10.80.0.40/443'
echo "TCP probe exit status: $?"
expected: Direct outside TCP 443 to the private IIS address is blocked with a matching firewall record, while the approved proxy request still succeeds.

title: Test the DMZ’s blocked management and domain paths
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console; FW01 Live View
expected: The DMZ can reach only the intended private HTTPS service; the tested RDP/SMB paths have matching deny logs.

title: Check the policy and adapter inventory together
where: Windows host browser · FW01 Live View and Workstation settings
expected: The connection matrix has both allowed and denied evidence, and the inventory shows no alternate route around FW01.

title: Correlate the request in proxy and IIS logs
where: PROXY01 terminal; IIS-DMZ01 → IIS Manager → DMZ-Lab → Logging
expected: The same labtrace request can be matched across proxy and IIS logs with the expected proxy/client distinction.

title: Create one controlled upstream failure
where: Windows host browser · FW01 DMZ rule list; TEST01 terminal
fields: Clear only matching proxy → IIS 443 states
Re-enable rule · Apply · retest both paths
expected: A deliberately blocked upstream is diagnosed from logs and recovered by restoring the single known rule.

title: Separate certificate errors from routing errors
where: PROXY01 · AlmaLinux console
command:
sudo nginx -t
systemctl status nginx --no-pager
getsebool httpd_can_network_connect
openssl x509 -in /etc/pki/tls/certs/iis-backend.pem -noout -subject -dates -ext subjectAltName
sudo tail -n 20 /var/log/nginx/dmz-error.log
expected: You can identify whether the fault is configuration, name/trust, time, service policy or a blocked network path.

title: Rehearse a clean rollback
where: Windows host · Workstation consoles and private change notes
expected: Your recovery notes identify the exact checkpoint, restore order and full validation matrix without touching AD.

where: Your notebook · Azure architecture planning

Private IIS VM · no public IP
expected: The Azure diagram separates managed ingress, private application and data/domain tiers, with no public IP on the backend VM.
